as_told: Soviet scientists drilling a very deep hole in Siberia broke through into a hollow space at about 14 km. The temperature there was about 2,000 degrees. They lowered a microphone and recorded the screams of people suffering in hell, and many of the workers quit in fear.
lesson: Science has found physical proof that hell is a real place under the earth.
what_happened: By 1990 the story was spread by the Trinity Broadcasting Network and a Texas evangelist. In 1990 the radio host Rich Buhler traced it. He found that the 'Finnish scientific journal' was a newsletter of Finnish missionaries, and that the trail went back through a reader's letter and a Helsinki Christian magazine to an unnamed 'Christian newsletter from California', where it stopped. The story names no real well. The deepest Soviet research well was the Kola Superdeep well (SG-3) on the Kola Peninsula in northwestern USSR, not in Siberia; that the story grew from news of this well is an inference by others, not a fact I could check. The published Soviet results for that well show ordinary rock heating with depth, temperature logs to 11,503 m, and a forecast of only 266 °C at 15,000 m.
false_part: No drillers broke into a hollow space or recorded screams; the only known deep Soviet research well recorded normal rock temperatures far below the 2,000 degrees in the story.

original.what: Same article: where Buhler's trail of the story ended
original.quote: thought he got it from a Christian newsletter from California

original.what: U.S. Geological Survey Open File Report 86-517, a detailed summary of Kozlovskiy's 1984 Soviet monograph on the Kola Superdeep well: location
original.who: James W. Clarke and others, U.S. Geological Survey
original.quote: Drilling of the Kola Superdeep well (SG-3) was begun in May, 1970 on the Kola Peninsula above the Arctic Circle in northwestern U.S.S.R.

original.what: Same report: measured temperature gradient and the forecast temperature at 15 km
original.who: James W. Clarke and others, U.S. Geological Survey
original.quote: Linear extrapolation of the geothermal gradient (0.019°C/m) gives a temperature of 266°C at a depth of 15,000 m in the Kola hole.

lesson_verdict.why: The real deep well was logged for temperature and showed rock warming steadily at about 2 °C per 100 m, with no hollow space; no record shows any sound from below.

source.what: U.S. Geological Survey Open File Report 86-517 (summary of Kozlovskiy 1984), geophysical logging section
source.quote: Logs were run to a depth of 11,503 m.

search_steps: Web search for the Well to Hell hoax, Ammennusastia, Trinity Broadcasting Network and Age Rendalen: found Wikipedia, Skeptoid and Snopes pages (leads only) and a 1991 Deseret News column by Jan Harold Brunvand.

Saved the Brunvand column (Deseret News, 15 May 1991). It is a lead: it names the TBN magazine Praise the Lord, February 1990, and Buhler's article in Christianity Today, 16 July 1990, and gives a geologist's guess that the story grew from news of the Kola well.
Saved Buhler's full article from christianitytoday.com (dated 1990-07-16 in the page data).
The Finnish newsletter Ammennusastia, the TBN broadcasts and the February 1990 Praise the Lord magazine are not online in full text; not obtained.

Searched for Rendalen's own account and the Secular Humanist Bulletin of October 1990: not found online. Rendalen's admission is known only as speech reported in Buhler's article, so I treated it as a lead.
Open Library and Chronicling America were not searched for this story because the story begins in 1989 and Chronicling America ends in 1963.

Searched for an open-access scientific record of the Kola well: found U.S. Geological Survey Open File Report 86-517 (1986), saved as PDF and text. Kozlovsky's Scientific American article of December 1984 is not free online.
Wayback snapshots found for the Christianity Today article and the USGS report.
confidence_note: The earliest telling I could read is a caller's version quoted by Buhler in July 1990; earlier versions on TBN and in Finnish newsletters exist but I could not read them. The well's final depth after 1984 is not in my saved sources. Rendalen's hoax letter is reported only by Buhler.
